decision_conditions: The proposed development seeks to introduce first floor rear extensions to the existing dwelling and the proposed dwelling. The description of development of the extant permission (ref. 24/03194/FUL) expressly refers to the 'erection of a two storey semi-detached dwelling house and single storey rear extension to existing dwelling'. The introduction of first floor rear extensions would therefore result in development that is materially different from that described in the original permission. Section 73 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 cannot be used to vary the description of development, and the proposal is not capable of being lawfully considered under this procedure. In this respect, the application is contrary to the principles established in Finney v Welsh Ministers [2019].

The flat-roofed first floor rear extension to the existing dwelling, by reason of its design, height, bulk, and roof form, would result in a visually discordant and poorly integrated addition that fails to respect the character and appearance of the host building and surrounding area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Chapter 12 of the NPPF (2024), Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) And policies DMD 6 and DMD 8 of the of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The dual-pitched first floor rear extension to the proposed new dwelling, by reason of its height, depth, and proximity to the boundary with No. 22A, would result in an overbearing form of development, causing harm to the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers. The application has not demonstrated that this impact would be acceptable. The proposal is therefore contrary to Chapter 12 of the NPPF (2024), Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) And policies DMD 6 and DMD 8 of the of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014)
